clue.text: Rejects and scoffs at make-up

indicators.note: make-up as a noun means composition, so these letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses things and mocks the cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics being scoffed at, but it is the anagram signal: SCOFFS AT is rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard or throw aside unwanted things, such as knitting stitches or garments, is to cast them off.

clue.text: A man surrounded by animals — does

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the man inside the animals

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by female deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like female deer, but it is the verb, as in 'does someone out of money'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them.

clue.text: Drink if apprehensive about blunder

indicators.note: about puts the first word round the second

explanation.surface: Have a drink if worried about making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: SHY goes 'about' ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Spain, an example of a drink.

clue.text: A model politician will be in Cheshire town

indicators.note: will be in puts the politician inside the town

parts.note: Sale is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: An exemplary MP is going to be in a north-west England town.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen or example, something representative of the rest.

clue.text: Prevents everyone going into the woods

indicators.note: going into puts everyone inside the woods

explanation.surface: Someone stops everyone heading for the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL goes 'into' FORESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to anticipate and pre-empt someone, blocking their move.

clue.text: A good man got into debt when laid up

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is the crossword's standard good man
someone who has got into debt owed money

explanation.surface: A virtuous man ran up debts while confined to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' suggests illness, but here it means put away in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods laid up are packed away in storage, as cargo is in a ship's hold.

clue.text: Warn theatre characters over a point

indicators.note: the characters (letters) are turned over, so they are rearranged

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Caution people in theatre about a point.
explanation.walkthrough: THEATRE is rearranged; N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to menace or intimidate, giving warning of harm.

clue.text: Stroll across and find it's child's play

explanation.surface: Walking over, someone finds a task easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy victory, with no real opposition; a doddle.

clue.text: Do without to give to others

definitions.meaning: to ... with something is to do without it

explanation.surface: Manage without something so as to share it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispense with means forgo; dispense alone means distribute, as a chemist hands out medicine.

clue.text: Till the cows come home nevertheless!

definitions.text: Till the cows come home nevertheless!

parts.words: Till the cows come home nevertheless!
parts.note: the idiom means for an endless time; the joke is that the opposite of 'never less' is '...'

explanation.surface: Someone insists on waiting indefinitely, come what may.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'nevertheless' as 'never ... less' and swap each half for its opposite to get the answer, which also means for all time, like the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the idiom and the answer mean for ever, for an unending stretch of time.

clue.text: Aims to get well?

parts.note: read not as a patient hoping to recover but as boring tools whose purpose is to sink a water or oil well

explanation.surface: A sick person's hopes of recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get well' suggests recovery from illness; the question mark warns that 'well' is a hole sunk in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring tools are used to sink wells for water or oil.

clue.text: Sits with reel spinning without wearying of it

indicators.note: something spinning is whirled round, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An angler sits winding a fishing reel all day without getting bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' fits the fishing picture of a reel turning, but it signals that SITS REEL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tireless effort never flags, carrying on with no sign of fatigue.

clue.text: Part after exchanging a quiet word

indicators.note: after puts the part at the end, behind the swapped pair
the two letters swap places, so the A and the P change round

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Actors trade a soft-spoken line after swapping parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging' swaps A and P to give PA; ROLE comes after it. The definition is 'word' as in a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner released on parole gives a word of honour to behave, the original sense of the French term.

clue.text: Brooding about nurse with foreboding

indicators.note: about puts the brooding round the nursing

explanation.surface: Someone broods over a nurse with dread.
explanation.walkthrough: PORING goes 'about' TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Portending means being an omen of something, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: They're under pressure to provide a weather-forecast

definitions.text: They're under pressure to provide a weather-forecast

parts.words: They're under pressure to provide a weather-forecast
parts.note: read literally: instruments that respond to atmospheric pressure and so indicate coming weather

explanation.surface: Forecasters are stressed by the demand to predict the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under pressure' suggests stressed people; literally, these instruments sit under air pressure and measure it.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments measuring atmospheric pressure, whose rise or fall hints at fair or stormy weather.

clue.text: Rock bottom price?

parts.note: read as the lowest price; but bottom is base, price is rate, giving a bank's reference interest rate

explanation.surface: A bargain at the cheapest possible price.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The central bank's lending rate, the bottom from which other charges for borrowing are set.

clue.text: Start with the guys caught in advance

indicators.note: in places the guys and the catch inside the advance

parts.note: to come on is to advance
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Begin with the men captured early.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN and C go 'in' COME.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence is to begin, get going.

clue.text: Carol holds colour to be limiting

indicators.note: holds means the carol keeps the colour inside

explanation.surface: A Christmas song has a restrictive colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name or a noun but is the verb sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinting means being sparing, giving little, holding back.

clue.text: Ministry defector, admitting nothing, left

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the defector takes the other letters inside

parts.note: an apostate is one who abandons a faith or party
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A government department's turncoat, confessing to nothing, has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministry' looks like a government department but means the office of an apostle. 'left' is not departed but L.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or mission of an apostle is a religious ministry, preaching the faith.

clue.text: Direction should be looked for

explanation.surface: A direction should be sought.
explanation.definitionFit: Past of seek: searched for.

clue.text: A number perhaps aren't absorbed

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Some figures perhaps haven't been taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is L (fifty); 'perhaps' rearranges AREN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge absorbed has been taken in and memorised.

clue.text: Given some support, didn't quit

definitions.meaning: a stay is a prop or support

explanation.surface: With some help, someone stuck it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a brace or strut, and staying means remaining.

clue.text: This man's mud slinging in consequence

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the other word

parts.note: an end is a result or consequence

indicators.note: slinging means throwing about, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A man indulges in mudslinging, with results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slinging' turns MUD into DMU, which goes 'in' END.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, as in the English king who was martyred; any named male fits 'this man'.

clue.text: At home alone with a good book that's really saucy

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
NT, the New Testament, is a good book in crossword terms

explanation.surface: A naughty novel read alone at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' in the surface suggests racy reading; in the definition it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is impudent and cheeky, an old sense of saucy.

clue.text: Set free to follow a relative

indicators.note: to follow puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: to untie is to set free from bonds

explanation.surface: A relative released after following someone.
explanation.walkthrough: UNTIE follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar word for a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: Urge turning around in trains with caution

indicators.note: around places the reversed word round the next piece
turning means the word for urge is read backwards

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
RLY is the abbreviation for railway, the trains

explanation.surface: Someone urges people to turn around carefully while on trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EGG to GGE, which goes 'around' IN to give GINGE; RLY (railway) finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gingerly means doing it carefully and warily.

clue.text: Issue some schemer generally raises

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A plotter usually produces some problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'schEMER GEnerally'; 'raises' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth is to come out or appear.

clue.text: Get aid at getting organisation wound up

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Get help from a charity that has been liquidated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' suggests a company closing; here it means tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wound up is nervous and on edge.
